source_inspection.title: The Cave Beneath the Sun Pyramid, Teotihuacan: Narrative of a Reverentially Terminated Mountain-Cave
source_inspection.publisher: University of Pittsburgh Center for Comparative Archaeology
source_inspection.inspected: Original full-text PDF selected printed pp.119–124 and 125–130; directly inspected original illustrated page 121, 123, 126, 128 and Table 8.1 p.129
source_inspection.not_inspected: Other chapters not exhaustively re-read; Gazzola 2016 laboratory analyses and individual original excavation inventories not independently inspected

findings.subject: Sun Pyramid cave terminal chamber: introduced minerals and worked slate
findings.statement: Sload documents more than 20 pieces of slate at the cave's eastern terminus, with only two likely slate pieces in a C:West Layer 5f rodent burrow outside that concentration; terminal specimens include pyrite-bearing slate and cleaved pieces with drilled holes, some interpreted cautiously as possible mirror backs or pendants. Magnetite from the B:West BYCT layer and gypsum from B:East excavation backdirt were also illustrated.
findings.site: Cave beneath the Sun Pyramid, Teotihuacan
findings.period: mainly Tzacualli–Miccaotli association inferred; deposition and reworking uncertain
findings.evidence_type: artifact inventory, photographs and investigator interpretation
findings.uncertainty: Mirror-back and pendant functional attributions speculative; exact terminal placement may be affected by earlier excavation/backdirt; pyrite alteration minerals on these individual pieces not chemically established; not independently corroborated
findings.educational_use: object investigation: pyrite-bearing slate and potential reflective objects in the Sun Pyramid cave

findings.subject: Sun Pyramid cave Area D ceramic censer associated with dated firepit
findings.statement: The TE28 Area D fire pit associated with charcoal determination Beta-220763 yielded a flower-pot censer rim and body fragment weighing 68.1 g. Sload illustrates a white post-firing wash and red fugitive pigment identified in the caption as cinnabar. The object may represent ritual use before emplacement of the overlying concrete floor; that activity sequence remains the excavator's interpretation.
findings.site: Cave beneath the Sun Pyramid, Teotihuacan, entrance Area D
findings.period: Tzacualli–Miccaotli or Miccaotli–Early Tlamimilolpa ceramic attribution debated
findings.evidence_type: excavated pottery fragment, photographs, ceramic attribution, radiocarbon-associated context
findings.uncertainty: Cinnabar is the author's reported pigment description, not verified here by compositional assay; charcoal dates activity context, not direct object manufacture; phase range not fixed
findings.educational_use: object dossier: painted censer rim and last-fire hypothesis

enrichments.subject: Ceramic types and contexts beneath Sun Pyramid
enrichments.statement: Sload's Table 8.1 subdivides the existing 273 TE28 sherds into 90 undisturbed and 183 disturbed: undisturbed counts are 33 ollas, 36 bowls, 8 jars, 9 plates/low dishes, 2 censers and 2 other/missing-data sherds; disturbed counts are 71 ollas, 39 bowls, 31 jars, 11 plates, 15 censers, 10 vases and 6 other. The 1977 surface collection adds 148 sherds, making the separately tabulated whole cave sample 421, not 421 TE28 sherds.
enrichments.uncertainty: Small condition-specific samples, disturbed provenience, no whole pots, typological identifications of individual sherds may be revised; descriptive counts only

issues.statement: No chemical assay of putative jarosite/limonite or pigment on specific reviewed slate/censer objects was inspected; separate Gazzola research cited by Sload is not independent confirmation here.
Original Sugiyama/Sugiyama/Sarabia 2013 Sun Pyramid sample-level Table 2 and figures remain unexamined; this batch does not resolve the Sun Pyramid construction chronology.
